format: uint8, layers x 20484, 0..255 = 0..1 within the scale (positive part only)

ebenen.name: Synchrony between viewers
ebenen.text: Where the brains of 30 people run in sync while they watch the same 14 short films. High: the film drives this area the same way in everyone. Low: everyone is thinking their own thoughts. This map is measured data.
ebenen.quelle: Emo-FilM, University of Geneva (Morgenroth et al. 2025, Sci Data, doi 10.1038/s41597-025-04803-5), CC0

ebenen.name: Where our model hits
ebenen.text: How well our own model predicts the brain response from image and sound for a film it has never seen (correlation per point, 4 held-out films, mean of 30 people). Strongest for hearing and voices, weak for valuation and reward.
ebenen.quelle: Emo-FilM, University of Geneva (Morgenroth et al. 2025, Sci Data, doi 10.1038/s41597-025-04803-5), CC0; model: tribe-lab/emofilm (SigLIP + Whisper, Ridge)

ebenen.name: Surprise
ebenen.text: Where the brain follows along when viewers rate a moment as “Surprise”: the link between second-by-second ratings from 44 people and the brain activity of 30 viewers across 14 films. Emotions overlap strongly, so the maps reflect “exciting vs. calm” more than any single emotion.
ebenen.quelle: Emo-FilM, University of Geneva (Morgenroth et al. 2025, Sci Data, doi 10.1038/s41597-025-04803-5), CC0, annotations ds004872 (CC0)
